{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before using the new credential update",
      "body": "The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the SafeParse result",
      "body": "parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the complete safeParse result, shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the credential object itself. Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use actual field validation instead of computed Zod object keys",
      "body": "Calling toString() on a Zod schema does not create a wildcard property matcher. Both computed keys evaluate to the literal '[object Object]', and the optional definition overwrites the numeric one. Because z.object strips unknown properties by default, a normal synced response loses expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other metadata. Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Preserve the adapters' refresh-result contracts on the sync path",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but the fallback returns whatever the provider client produces. Google and both Zoho adapters immediately read result.data, while HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly; none of those properties exists on a fetch Response. Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Send the credential owner's user ID rather than the credential ID",
      "body": "The third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. Credential IDs and user IDs identify different records, so the external store can either fail the lookup or return another user's OAuth token, which is then saved on this credential. Passing a credential ID also bypasses the helper's intended exclusion of team-owned credentials. Thread credential.userId into this call."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder",
      "body": "This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's native response schema explicitly permits an omitted refresh_token, and its caller merges the parsed response into the existing credential. Previously that preserved the current refresh token; now the literal string 'refresh_token' overwrites it. The next native refresh submits that placeholder and fails, requiring the user to reconnect. Leave an omitted refresh token absent so callers can retain the existing value."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests",
      "body": "The request to the external token broker contains only a guessable calcomUserId and appSlug, with no authentication header or other caller credential. For an Internet-reachable sync endpoint, requests generated by this protocol are indistinguishable from requests made by an attacker seeking another user's access token. An endpoint enforcing shared-secret authentication would instead reject every refresh. Add an authenticated exchange, such as sending the configured shared secret in the configured header."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Use the canonical Zoom app slug in sync requests",
      "body": "This sends appSlug='zoomvideo', but Zoom credentials are created with appId='zoom' and its app keys are also looked up using 'zoom'. 'zoomvideo' is the integration directory name, not the app-store slug used by the new webhook contract. An external store indexing credentials by the canonical app slug cannot resolve this request, so Zoom token synchronization fails."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "The newly added refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never uses refreshOAuthTokens. Even when credential sharing and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, Salesforce therefore ignores the platform designated as the credential source of truth and still requires a usable local refresh token. Platform-managed credentials cannot follow the new refresh flow. Apply the same user/team-aware sync routing used by the other adapters."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Handle the access-token-only sync response in Webex and Lark",
      "body": "The shared helper documents a sync response containing only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates it with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires scope, token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A compliant sync response is therefore rejected before its token is used, breaking Webex operations once the old token expires. Lark has the same mismatch: it expects nested data.data and refresh-token metadata. These adapters need sync-specific response handling rather than retaining native OAuth response requirements."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Use the refreshed Salesforce token for the current connection",
      "body": "The new refresh result is written to the database but never applied to credentialKey. The jsforce.Connection constructed immediately afterward still receives the original access_token and instance_url. If the original token is expired, the current operation uses that expired token and jsforce must refresh again despite the successful refresh just performed. Initialize the connection from the refreshed values instead of adding a redundant token request and database write."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 83,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make webhook credential creation idempotent under concurrent delivery",
      "body": "Finding an existing credential and creating one are separate, unsynchronized operations. Two concurrent first deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create separate rows. Subsequent deliveries update only one row through findFirst, leaving another installed credential with stale tokens. Serialize the keyed find-or-create operation or use an appropriate uniqueness and retry mechanism so concurrent webhook delivery cannot create duplicate credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear the invalid flag when replacing invalid credentials",
      "body": "Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credential rows invalid=true after an invalid_grant. When the source platform reconnects an account and sends working replacement keys, this webhook finds the existing row and changes only key, leaving invalid=true. The refreshed integration remains marked invalid despite the successful sync response and cannot be restored through this endpoint without deleting or reinstalling it. Reset the invalid state when accepting replacement credentials."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before using the new credential update
findings.body: The new code calls prisma.credential.update, but this module neither imports nor declares prisma. This fails TypeScript checking and, in builds that skip type checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the database update.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials rather than the SafeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the complete safeParse result, shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous schema.parse call returned the credential object itself. Saving that result as credential.key moves all OAuth fields under data. The next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot read the stored access token, refresh token, or expiry at their expected locations, breaking the integration after a successful refresh even when credential sharing is disabled.

findings.title: Use actual field validation instead of computed Zod object keys
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema does not create a wildcard property matcher. Both computed keys evaluate to the literal '[object Object]', and the optional definition overwrites the numeric one. Because z.object strips unknown properties by default, a normal synced response loses expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, and other metadata. Zoom then calculates its expiry from undefined, while Office365 retains an already-expired value. Preserve and validate the actual response fields.

Consequently, even a successful JSON response from the sync endpoint causes exceptions or undefined token values for these integrations. Decode and normalize the remote response, and adapt the callers to a consistent result contract.
